name: security-npm-publication-provenance-review
intent: npm trusted-publisher identity and alternate package publication paths
artifacts: Publisher permissions, trusted publishing configuration, build workflow and produced package digest/provenance.
trace: Trace which repository/workflow/environment can publish the package and whether provenance corresponds to the exact consumed artifact rather than a different run.
experiment: Compare the package registered trusted-publisher CI identity with a mismatched repository/workflow/environment and an alternate legacy publishing credential path using supplied configuration and offline artifacts. Do not publish or install a package.
disproof: A provenance badge or package metadata field alone is not verified release trust; do not publish a conflicting public package to test it.
repair: Bind publication to intended workflow identity and verify artifact provenance at the release consumer.
branch_decisions: Separate publisher authentication, package ownership, artifact integrity and provenance subject identity. An attestation can accurately describe a malicious but authorized build; it does not replace source trust. Bind the actual registry tarball digest to the expected repository/workflow identity, and do not publish a test package or install untrusted lifecycle scripts for verification.
operational_method: Inspect the package registered trusted-publisher identity: CI provider, repository/project, workflow and any configured environment. Bind that identity to the OIDC exchange and actual package/version publication; provenance subject digest matching is a separate check. Record remaining legacy automation tokens or publish paths that bypass the intended publisher restriction. Use supplied registry/publisher records and offline artifacts; do not publish a package or infer source review from an accurate attestation.
